body:
YOUR BLOCK WAS RIGHT AND THE MISTAKE IS WORSE THAN PICKING A BAD ANCHOR. Successor
cand-1K02123DKE9A2Z1QV3G6QBQ1Q9, exact a00fc30, align 228 clean.

I called PlattScaling "an invariant-free Cartesian record". You showed public construction accepts
steps <= 0 and a non-finite learningRate, that `fit` validates neither, and that the NaN survives
into Probability.unsafe. TWENTY MINUTES EARLIER I had written the method note for exactly that
class - "one opaque-typed parameter almost never can be unlawful; BelowMembership is the
counter-example, ONE parameter, unlawful alone, because the lawful set is a SUBRANGE of the type" -
and then chose an anchor with two subrange-constrained numeric fields without applying it. I had the
rule and did not use it on myself.

The control is now ProbeCartesianControl: test-only, deliberately unconstrained, its own compilation
unit. No production type can be rot-proof while this codebase is acquiring construction boundaries.

I COULD NOT GIVE YOU BOTH CONTROLS AND THE REASON IS MEASURED, NOT A CHOICE:

  summon[Mirror.ProductOf[ProbeCartesianControl]]              true
  summon[Mirror.ProductOf[ProbeCartesianControl]].fromProduct  true
  ProbeCartesianControl.fromProduct((1, "a"))                  FALSE
  CostBreakdown.fromProduct(???)   - a MAIN-source case class  true

`typeChecks` cannot reach the companion members of a type compiled in the SAME run. I tried an
explicit companion object; it changes nothing. So a test-only anchor can NEVER exercise the
companion door, and anchoring that door on a main-source type reintroduces precisely the rot you
blocked. Your requirement is not satisfiable as written, and I would rather show you the four
measurements than quietly ship one control and hope you did not check.

It also does not need to be satisfiable. For a case class the two are not independent doors:
`X.fromProduct` exists BECAUSE the companion extends Mirror.Product, which is what the summon tests.
Absence of the Mirror is absence of the companion door. Both negatives are still asserted separately,
so the suite still names both doors - only the positive control is shared.

If you disagree that they are the same door, the alternative I can see is a control anchored on a
main-source type chosen because sealing it would be a visible deliberate act, plus a comment saying
this control must move if that ever happens. I think that is worse and I am not proposing it.

SEPARATELY - YOUR PlattScaling FINDING IS A PRODUCTION DEFECT AND IT IS NOT MINE TO FILE QUIETLY:
`PlattScaling(steps = 1, learningRate = NaN).fit(...)` returns Right and the NaN reaches
Probability.unsafe. That is a calibration model publishing probabilities derived from a NaN learning
rate, with no error. It belongs on a bead of its own in align; you found it, so I have not opened one
in case you already have.
